mintCallSequence.op: require(amount > 0, 'Amount must be greater than zero')

mintFailureModesAsSeenByAntimatter: Every branch above is a REVERT, never a reduced payout. calculateMintAmountBackground.status: NO LONGER CALLED BY ANTIMATTER — background only
calculateMintAmountBackground.zeroCases: returns 0 for an unregistered stablecoin (exchangeRate 0) and for a registered one whose exchangeRate the owner has set to 0. Under c91bc1a this was caught pre-burn by PhUSDNotReceived; at 3a96fb7 nothing catches it except the caller's own minPhUSDOut, and only if that floor exceeds `amount`.
calculateMintAmountBackground.rounding: the division by 1e18 at line 255 truncates toward zero
calculateMintAmountBackground.authorNote: line 252-253 carries an explicit note-to-auditors that >18-decimal stablecoins are assumed not to exist; Antimatter independently enforces decimals <= 18 at Antimatter.sol:289.

initialValue.note: exchangeRate is set from the caller's argument; enabled defaults to true and maxMintPerDay defaults to 0 (uncapped) — lines 120-128

exchangeRateMutability.relevanceToTheDelta: The rate is owner-mutable at any time and there is no timelock, no bound, and no event-driven guard. Antimatter's NatSpec (Antimatter.sol:215-218) explicitly accepts this as legitimate. Combined with the deletion of the quote comparison, the rate in force at the moment minter.mint lands is the sole determinant of the stable half's payout, checked only against the caller's combined-total floor. Adjudication deferred to interaction/econ analysis.
